result.message: Reviewed the round-3 candidate (subject sha256 d041edc0…, identical to .best_kernel.py and ledger round-3 solution) against the supplied catalog (definition/oracle/19 workloads) and the optimize ledger measurements. The candidate is a legitimate Triton implementation of gelu_and_mul: it allocates its own output (no mutation/alias), keeps the catalog ABI (single positional hidden_states, one output, run = gelu_and_mul), never calls torch.nn.functional/torch.ops, performs no host synchronization, sets no environment state, and contains no workload-UUID or shape-table special casing. Ten of the catalog's graded shapes were also used in the ledger measurements, but the code paths (_tile_shape, cache key, grid) are generic formulas, not shape lookups. Two advisory P1 concerns remain: (1) the kernel computes the tanh/sigmoid approximation of GELU while the catalog reference is exact-erf `F.gelu(..., approximate="none")` and the definition/oracle imposes no dtype restriction, so the substitution is only justified by an on-target probe claim in the docstring and would exceed the catalog's own float32 tolerance (1e-4) if any fp32/fp64 case were ever graded; (2) the cached direct-launch path keys only on (dtype, num_rows, half, input/output alignment residue) and not on device, and depends on a build-specific non-public CompiledKernel launch ABI/signature pinned by trial-and-error in the ledger, with broad `except Exception` shielding that can repeatedly pay a failed cached attempt. Performance PASSED (geo_mean 2.2671, min_speedup 1.9229) in the ledger is consistent with the candidate reducing real per-call launch work (it re-issues the kernel each call and never memoizes results). No P0 code finding; no evidence of prohibited fallback, measurement bypass, or test-specific values.
